scene.note: The boat's fields are private, so the only way on or off is through methods that keep the seat rule.

steps.note: Each boat keeps its name, its seats and who is aboard, where only its own code can reach.
Anyone may ask a boat its name, its seats and how many are aboard, through its methods.
A line outside the boat that tries to change a field is refused before the program runs.
Passengers come aboard one by one, and some land again before the boat leaves.
While a seat is free, the passenger goes on the list. On a full boat, nothing changes and the answer is no.
Someone landing comes off the list by name, and their seat is free again. A name nobody has is a no.
The boat's own list says who is aboard, in the order they boarded.
The harbour office gets a list of its own with the same names.
Whatever the office writes on its copy, the boat's list stays as it was.
Printed as it is, a boat shows only its class name and a code.
With a text of its own, printing a boat shows its name, how many are aboard and the seats free.
